newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Camdessus says IMF to decide Pakistan loan "soon".
newsitem.headline: Camdessus says IMF to decide Pakistan loan "soon".

text.p: The International Monetary Fund was discussing a standby loan with Pakistan and would make a decision in the next few days, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday.
Pakistan has been negotiating an agreement with the IMF over a stalled $600 million standby loan considered crucial for shoring up the nation's finances.
"We will have to make this judgement in the next few days and then you will hear about our decision," Camdessus told reporters during a two-day conference on macroeconomic issues.

Camdessus said the IMF programme with Pakistan went off track last month, well before President Farooq Leghari sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto on Tuesday. Leghari accused Bhutto's government of corruption and misrule.
Camdessus said the IMF and the Pakistani authorities were working hard to put together a programme which should bring Pakistan back on course in its reforms.
"We were discussing that and finalising a programme when the president decided to dismiss Miss Bhutto," Camdessus said.
"We are indeed continuing our work. We have to assess the situation to make a judgement on the possibility during the next few months and particularly before the next election."
"You certainly understand that a few hours after this political change I can not tell you what will be our final decision," Camdessus said.
